purpose: Preserve distinct mechanisms recovered from literal exported ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Gemini histories after deduplication and comparison against Garden v15.5 plus the existing historical-chat recovery, KR-CEA and active v15.6 candidate sets. No private chat text is published.

archive_audit_boundary.method: Every normalized message was mechanically parsed/indexed; long-lived chats were split by message time; repeated long user payloads were hash-deduplicated across agents; high-signal design sessions were reviewed in bounded chronological passes. Pasted AI text was treated as artifact provenance, not automatically as human belief.
archive_audit_boundary.privacy: Only abstract mechanisms and coarse provenance are retained here. No private personal assertions or verbatim private-chat excerpts are published.

candidates.title: Hazard-monotonic emergency action selection
candidates.historical_provenance: Early GAIA safety-control lineage, February 2026, independently iterated across the exported agent histories.
candidates.current_overlap: v15.5 already has HazardPredicate, SafetyEnvelope, EmergencyAdmissionContract, bounded SafeActionSet, authority/scope/expiry, recovery and audit. The residual is an explicit selection/dominance rule inside an already-authorized emergency action set.
candidates.problem: Ordinary comfort/performance/nominal limits can conflict with immediate hazard reduction. A safe system should not reject a stronger pre-authorized emergency action merely because it exceeds an ordinary soft limit when that action demonstrably reduces the controlling hazard and remains inside all higher-priority hard bounds.
candidates.minimal_change: Within an already valid EmergencyAdmissionContract, permit candidate actions to be compared by typed hazard deltas. An action may relax only declared soft/ordinary bounds when it is inside the pre-authorized emergency envelope, lowers the controlling hazard under the declared model/uncertainty treatment, and violates no Constitution/rights/K0P/authority/physical hard invariant. Preserve incomparability/UNKNOWN and safe fallback when dominance is not established.
hard_limits: Never creates emergency authority.
Never relaxes Constitution/rights/K0P/authority or physical hard invariants.
Reducing one hazard cannot hide creation of a higher-priority hazard.
Model uncertainty and stale calibration remain explicit; no fabricated monotonicity.
tests: Emergency braking beyond an ordinary comfort bound is admissible only when already authorized, physically safe and hazard-reducing.
A candidate that reduces collision risk but violates a higher-priority structural hard bound is rejected.
When hazard ordering is incomparable or model uncertainty exceeds the profile bound, the selector returns UNKNOWN/SAFE_FALLBACK rather than inventing dominance.

candidates.title: Versioned unsafe-region / infeasibility memory for planning reuse
candidates.historical_provenance: Early GAIA iterations repeatedly introduced bounded memory of infeasible/dangerous control regions so later planning could avoid rediscovering the same failure.
candidates.current_overlap: Garden already stores counterexamples/corrections and KR-CEA preserves provenance, contradiction, lineage and revalidation. The residual is a typed state/action/trajectory-region representation usable as a scoped planning-pruning constraint rather than only a textual counterexample.
candidates.minimal_change: Represent a proven or evidence-supported unsafe/infeasible region as a scoped knowledge candidate carrying domain/state variables, action/trajectory bounds, evidence/proof class, assumptions, validity interval, model/version binding, uncertainty margin, falsifiers and revalidation triggers. Retrieval may prune or penalize future search only within the recorded applicability scope.
hard_limits: One failure does not create a universal prohibition.
Statistical association is not promoted to physical impossibility without applicable causal/proof obligations.
Version/context/model changes trigger revalidation before reuse.
Rights or authority cannot be inferred from a no-go region.
tests: A formally proven infeasible control region is reused under the same bound model without full rediscovery.
A changed vehicle/model/environment invalidates or narrows a stale no-go region.
A noisy adverse outcome is retained as evidence/counterexample but cannot silently become a hard forbidden region.

candidates.title: Adversarial precedent revalidation for the pending justice workstream
candidates.historical_provenance: May 2026 Digital Garden governance lineage proposed periodically re-testing settled normative precedents rather than allowing accumulated precedent to become self-sealing.
candidates.current_overlap: HCA-007 already preserves the end-to-end justice pipeline and hard epistemic/due-process separations. HCA-002 covers behavioral/normative drift generally. This item specializes revalidation to precedent/case-law-like normative memory.
candidates.minimal_change: For high-impact or dependency-central precedents, support bounded revalidation triggers such as materially changed law, evidence, facts, social/technical context, conflicting later decisions, measured disparate effects, or held-out adversarial replay. Revalidation may preserve, narrow, distinguish, supersede or reopen a precedent; it does not automatically reverse outcomes or create punishment authority.
hard_limits: Finality, reliance interests, jurisdiction, appeal rules and lawful retroactivity constraints remain explicit.
Random disagreement alone does not reopen every case.
No AI-only re-litigation can bypass legally required human process.
Protected personal data is minimized and purpose-limited.
tests: A precedent whose governing law has materially changed is flagged for scoped revalidation.
A stable precedent is not reopened merely because another model votes differently.
Revalidation findings cannot silently alter a final judgment where lawful procedure requires a separate appeal/review path.

candidates.title: Change-complexity and assurance-burden accounting for upgrades
candidates.historical_provenance: From the earliest GAIA refinement loop onward, upgrades were repeatedly constrained by explicit size/complexity budgets while seeking maximum safety/function gain.
candidates.current_overlap: GCL already normalizes effect by intervention measure and Garden already checks lifecycle/cost/resource/testability. No new causal-leverage theory is needed.
candidates.minimal_change: For engineering/design deltas, optionally publish a ChangeComplexityReceipt decomposing semantic surface added/removed, dependency fan-out, code/spec delta, runtime/resource delta, migration cost, new verification obligations and long-term maintenance burden. Feed that typed measure into existing Compare/GCL rather than treating raw line count as universal complexity.
hard_limits: A small diff is not automatically safer or better.
Security/safety/rights requirements cannot be rejected merely to satisfy a complexity budget.
Metrics must not Goodhart into code-golf or hidden complexity.
tests: Two functionally equivalent upgrades can be compared on declared assurance/migration burden, not only LOC.
A tiny diff with large dependency fan-out is not mislabeled low-complexity.
A required safety fix remains admissible even when it exceeds a nominal complexity budget, with the excess explicitly recorded.

candidates.title: Temporal authority snapshot / anti-retroactive authorization binding
candidates.historical_provenance: June-July 2026 Digital Garden transaction/event architecture: cross-agent review explicitly separated claim/event valid time from the authority snapshot used at actual acceptance/linearization, to prevent backdated records from gaining permissions retroactively.
candidates.current_overlap: v15.5 already distinguishes semantic Version from time/context/scope Validity and requires scoped, expiring, revocable authority with provenance. The residual is an explicit binding rule for consequential admission: the authority/policy state used to authorize an accepted transition must be tied to the declared authoritative acceptance/linearization boundary, rather than silently inferred from a backdated event/claim valid time.
candidates.minimal_change: For consequential admissions whose legality/permission depends on time-varying authority, bind an immutable AuthorizationEvaluationContext containing the authoritative acceptance/linearization time or domain-equivalent commit boundary; policy/authority/credential/delegation snapshot identifiers; actor/context/jurisdiction; and the separately represented event/valid time. A historical or backdated Claim may describe a past-valid fact but cannot thereby manufacture permission that was absent at acceptance. Where law explicitly permits retroactive legal effect, represent that as a separately authorized domain rule/decision rather than falsifying the authorization timestamp.
hard_limits: Does not create authority and does not expand any credential/delegation scope.
Does not require one global clock or global linearization point; use the domain's declared authoritative admission/commit boundary.
Does not prohibit lawfully retroactive statutes, judgments, corrections or accounting effects; their retroactive effect must itself be authorized and represented explicitly.
Historical replay may evaluate the historical snapshot for explanation, but replay cannot silently create current execution authority.
Revocation/expiry races and distributed-clock uncertainty must follow a declared cutover/profile rule or remain BLOCKED/UNKNOWN rather than choosing the more permissive time silently.
tests: A transfer submitted after a credential was revoked cannot regain execution permission by declaring a valid_time from before revocation.
A historical observation accepted today may retain its past event/valid time as evidence without acquiring present action authority.
A lawfully retroactive adjudication is represented as a currently authorized decision with an explicit retroactive-effect rule, not as a forged earlier acceptance time.

When revocation and acceptance ordering cannot be established within the declared temporal profile, consequential admission returns BLOCKED/UNKNOWN instead of silently selecting the permissive snapshot.

confirmed_subsumed_or_already_tracked: Cross-agent copied text must not count as independent corroboration: already covered by KR-CEA lineage/non-amplification rules and source-independence hardening.
Unknown/inconclusive states must not be forced to PASS: already core Garden/GSL assurance behavior.
Small deterministic safety kernel plus adaptive outer cognition: already represented across current assurance/adapter/physical-safety machinery.
Independent multi-agent review and cross-examination: already repository and Garden evolution policy.
Behavior/mechanism drift, human-review workload, cross-scale causal search and outcome-based memory utility: already preserved in HISTORICAL-CHAT-RECOVERY.
Runtime epistemic assimilation, compression, retrieval reuse and model consolidation separation: already preserved in KR-CEA.
historical_ideas_not_promoted: Majority or model vote as a substitute for evidence/truth.
Frozen universal cultural-content rules as constitutional truth.
Punitive preference or popularity as automatic justice authority.
Randomized authority selection as a general solution to governance regress.
Claims of certification, regulatory compliance, economic savings or physical performance without supporting evidence.
A new top-level module merely to preserve a historical name.
promotion_boundary: This file preserves candidates only. Admission requires current whole-source equivalence/collision review, GSL-COMPARE including DO_NOTHING and stronger alternatives, independent same-target review, rights/privacy/authority analysis, executable tests/proofs where applicable, reference closure, and explicit human canonical promotion.
